UrbanPulse: Satellite Urban Sprawl & Land Cover Intelligence

High-resolution multi-temporal satellite analytics engine tracking urban sprawl, concentric ring densification, and Shannon entropy across metropolitan regions using Sentinel-2 and ESA WorldCover.

🌐 Live Web Dashboard 💻 GitHub Repository 📅 Generated: 2026-10-03 13:56 UTC 🔖 Git Commit: a5b7f43a ✔ CI/CD: Passing

🔍 1. Problem & Approach

Rapid urbanization across major metropolitan regions frequently outpaces civic planning frameworks, leading to unchecked peripheral sprawl, fragmentation of agricultural zones, and loss of critical blue-green infrastructure. Monitoring these dynamics using ad-hoc, single-scene satellite imagery often introduces severe seasonal phenological confusion, cloud contamination, and sensor baseline artifacts that corrupt time-series measurements.

UrbanPulse was engineered as an automated, reproducible Earth Observation (EO) pipeline. It harmonizes multi-temporal Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance datasets using STAC queries, computes pixel-level median composites over dry-season windows, trains spatial-block-balanced Random Forest classifiers against ESA WorldCover labels, and enforces strict temporal consistency rules (majority filtering and urban persistence) to deliver stable, high-fidelity spatial sprawl analytics.

🛠 2. System Architecture

The end-to-end data flow spanning satellite catalog ingestion, radiometric processing, machine learning classification, PostGIS spatial ingestion, and containerized deployment.

📊 3. Data & Methodology

Earth Observation Data Specifications

  • Sensor: Sentinel-2 Multi-Spectral Instrument (MSI), Level-2A Bottom-Of-Atmosphere (BOA) surface reflectance via AWS Earth Search STAC.
  • Spatial Resolution: 60.0 m analytical pixel grid (EPSG:32643 UTM projection), with 10.0 m high-resolution visual previews.
  • Area of Interest (AOI): 45.0 × 45.0 km bounding envelope centered on the municipal core (571,536 grid pixels per city).
  • Dry-Season Compositing: November 1 to February 28 window (with automated 1-month seasonal widening if valid observations < 4).
  • Cloud & Shadow Masking: SCL (Scene Classification Layer) masking cloud shadow, medium/high probability cloud, cirrus, and snow with 1-pixel binary dilation.
  • Radiometric Harmonization: Explicit scale (0.0001) and offset (-0.1) normalization compensating for the European Space Agency Sentinel-2 Processing Baseline 04.00 shift post-January 2022.

Machine Learning & Temporal Consistency

  • Spectral Feature Stack (8 Bands): Blue, Green, Red, NIR, SWIR16, plus spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI).
  • Supervised Classifier: Random Forest (200 trees, class_weight="balanced") pooled across reference years (2018, 2021, 2024).
  • Training Labels: ESA WorldCover 10m v200 (2021) mapped to 5 standardized classes (Built-up, Vegetation, Water, Agriculture, Open Land).
  • Spatial Block Partitioning: 8-fold non-overlapping spatial grid partition guaranteeing zero spatial autocorrelation between train and test folds.
  • Spatial Filtering: 3 × 3 majority mode filter applied to raw raster predictions to eliminate salt-and-pepper noise.
  • Temporal Consistency Rules:
    1. Majority Rule: Pixel is Built-up in year t only if Built-up in ≥ 2 of (t-1, t, t+1).
    2. Urban Persistence: Once Built-up for 2 consecutive years, pixels permanently stay Built-up (urban land persistence assumption).
    3. Modal Non-Built-Up: Filtered false-urban pixels receive their multi-year non-built-up modal class.

Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) Validation (Evaluated on ALL Held-Out Points)

To evaluate temporal stability without data leakage, classifiers were trained excluding each fold year, and tested on all held-out points (not restricted to stable points). Area estimates are adjusted using Olofsson et al. (2014) area-weighted stratified estimation with 95% confidence intervals.

⚠ Negative Result Notice (Radiometric Normalisation):

Cross-year Total Least Squares (TLS) pseudo-invariant feature radiometric normalisation was implemented and systematically tested. Empirical evaluation across all held-out test points demonstrates that radiometric normalisation did not reduce year-to-year drift compared to the baseline composite series. Consequently, rule-based temporal consistency filtering remains the authoritative operational mechanism for ensuring monotonic urban expansion.

How to Add a New Metropolitan Region

UrbanPulse is 100% configuration-driven. Add configs/<city>.yaml with the exact keys: 

city:
  name: Jaipur
  state: Rajasthan
  country: India
spatial:
  bbox: [75.6000, 26.7000, 76.0500, 27.1500]
  crs: EPSG:4326
  center_lat: 26.9124
  center_lon: 75.7873
  aoi_size_km: 45.0
temporal:
  analysis_years:
    start_year: 2018
    end_year: 2024
  dry_season:
    start_month: 11
    end_month: 2
    start_day: 11-01
    end_day: 02-28
stac:
  earth_search_url: https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1
  collections:
    sentinel_2: sentinel-2-c1-l2a

⚠ 7. Limitations

  • accuracy is agreement with ESA WorldCover, not field-verified ground truth
  • Sentinel-2 covers 2017 onward only
  • dry-season composites confuse fallow farmland with built-up land
  • the model is not transferable across sensors
  • the persistence rule forces non-decreasing built-up area and is a documented assumption
  • 10-60 m resolution limits small features.

🚀 8. Future Roadmap

1. Historical Landsat Integration (2000–2016)

Extend the temporal horizon by 16 years using harmonized Landsat 5/7/8 surface reflectance stacks with cross-calibration regression.

2. CA-Markov 2035 Urban Growth Forecasting

Couple Cellular Automata and Markov Transition Chains with slope, transport proximity, and zoning constraint layers for 2035 sprawl forecasting.

3. Hand-Labelled Ground-Truth Validation Set

Digitize high-resolution aerial imagery ground truth across 500 stratified random points to measure real-world precision beyond global maps.

4. Dynamic "Run This City" API Endpoint

Expose asynchronous Celery / Redis worker endpoints allowing users to submit any arbitrary bounding box for on-demand sprawl computation.

🔁 9. Reproducibility & Verification

All pipelines, tests, and documentation artifacts can be executed locally or in containerized environments with standard commands: 

# 1. Start full local stack (Web + API + DB + Prometheus)
make up

# 2. Run complete pipeline for a specific city and target year
make pipeline CITY=pune YEAR=2024

# 3. Execute standalone Python pipeline CLI
python -m pipeline.run_city --city ahmedabad

# 4. Run automated test suite
pytest -v

# 5. Re-generate this documentation and PDF report
make docs
